pr.title: Keep a pull request's row the same when its drawer opens
pr.head: 1557242883e21ae338a64b70b74ab998ae4a1bf7

summary: Projector's mod draws a panel above the Claude Code prompt that lists the pull requests your session fixes or reviews, one row each. A row shows the pull request's number, its state (the first status that applies, such as failing, changes, or findings), its title, and then notes: every other status that applies, such as clean or passing. Pressing a row's number opens its drawer beneath it, which shows the branch, the size of the change, the checks, the labels, and the unresolved review threads.

Before this change, opening the drawer also rewrote the row above it. The notes spelled holds out in full (checks failing, changes requested), added the hold that was already the row's state, and turned passing into checks passing. So the line you clicked changed shape as the drawer opened, and its last note repeated the drawer's facts line directly below.

Now a row's notes read the same open or closed. They keep their short forms, and no note repeats the state. The drawer's facts line still gives the checks in full, such as checks failing. The change removes the phrase field on each hold and the drawer argument to notesOf, updates the test to check that opening any drawer changes no row, and updates the panel documentation and its example.

cards.title: Merged with the blank-line change
cards.html: The branch merges in main, which now puts a blank line between your pull requests and the review requests. The two changes met only in the example panel in docs/plugins.md, where main added the blank line directly above the #258 row this change edits. The resolution keeps both: the blank line, then the #258 row ending in reviewing · passing, with its age in the same column as the row above. hooks/register.tsx and hooks/panel.test.tsx merged without a conflict, and this change's hunks in them are the same as before the merge.

groups.title: A row's notes no longer depend on its drawer
groups.kicker: notesOf drops its drawer argument, and each hold keeps one word
intro: HOLDS lists what holds a pull request back, most urgent first: conflict, failing, changes, and findings. rowState takes the first that holds as the row's state, and notesOf lists every other status after the title. Each hold used to carry an optional phrase, its long form, which notesOf used while the row's drawer was open.

Now notesOf takes only the pull request. A hold becomes a note exactly when it holds and is not the state, as review labels and draft already did, so the same row draws the same notes whichever drawer is open.

files.note: Removes phrase from Hold and HOLDS, drops the isOpen argument from notesOf and its one caller in drawRow, and always writes passing.

checks.text: No note can repeat the state: holds and review labels are filtered against rowState(pr).text, draft shows only when the state is not draft, and approved, passing, and cancelled are never a state. Checked by reading rowState and notesOf at the head.
drawRow is the only caller of notesOf, and nothing else read phrase. Checked by searching the hooks module and site/src.

groups.title: The test opens drawers and compares every row
groups.kicker: One loop replaces the assertions that pinned the long forms
intro: The panel test that lists each row's notes reads every row closed, then opens five drawers in turn and checks that every row's notes stay exactly as they were. The five cover a row failing its checks, one with changes requested, one whose state is findings, one whose state is failing, and one whose checks pass.

files.note: Renames the test and replaces the open-drawer assertions with a loop that compares all rows against their closed notes.

checks.text: The test catches a row that changes as its drawer opens: with the base's hooks/register.tsx under the head's tests, claude plugin test . fails this test alone (236 pass, 1 fail).

groups.title: The panel documentation describes the steady row
intro: The paragraph on a row's notes now says that no note repeats the state and that opening a drawer leaves the row as it was, with the drawer's facts line giving the checks in full. The example panel's open row ends in reviewing · passing, and its title is longer, so the line keeps its width.
